scope: Catalog sorting keys, directions, sentinel values, stability, and post-sort state

evidence.direction: The selected global-column bit is toggled before sorting; raw bit 0 is ascending and bit 1 descending, with an optional item-property reversal predicate
evidence.comparison: The generic comparator uses numeric comparison, formatted text when both left-aligned values are -1, and orders -3 after valid values in both directions
evidence.stability: The merge selects the left half on equality and copies complete 8-byte object/state pairs
evidence.post_sort_state: Stored selection and disablement move with objects; current index and scroll offset are not rewritten by sort or visible-row refresh
evidence.cross_domain: Tactic sort-key mapping is identity; person display keys 0 and 3 map to key 5, and person keys 3, 5, 16, 18, and 90 reverse effective direction

function_recovery.note: Recovered person sort-property mapper from item-vtable reference and validated code boundary
Recovered catalog refresh dispatcher from specialized dialog-vtable reference and validated code boundary

ida_changes.read_back: All eight names were visible after save; decompilation also retained the sorting, sentinel, refresh, and state comments

conclusion: Catalog sorting is a stable property-key sort with domain mapping and direction reversal hooks. Stored entry state follows object identity, while current and viewport state preserve numeric positions.
